source.title: MachineLearningLM: Scaling Many-shot In-context Learning via Continued Pretraining
source.authors: Haoyu Dong; Pengkun Zhang; Mingzhe Lu; Yanzhen Shen; Guolin Ke

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and table layouts have extraction artifacts, but the results relevant here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It reports downstream accuracy under a different scaling variable—number of in-context demonstrations—rather than testing the parameter/token/compute loss laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy as the number of in-context examples increases. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy against parameter count, training tokens, or training compute; extrapolation of loss laws; or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its discussion of other scaling-law work cites results from other papers, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study scales the number of in-context demonstrations, not parameters, tokens, compute or pretraining loss. It reports no pretraining loss curves and no model-size sweep, and uses a single 7B backbone. Its 'many-shot scaling law' is a different construct: accuracy versus demonstration count. Scaling-law work (e.g. TabDPT) appears only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that continued pretraining on synthetic SCM tabular tasks gives monotonic many-shot ICL accuracy gains (8 to 1,024 shots), near random-forest-level accuracy, and preserved MMLU (75.4%). They make no claims about parameter, token or compute laws.
record.recipe_differences: Continued pretraining with LoRA on synthetic SCM-generated tabular classification tasks and evaluation by in-context-shot accuracy; unlike the cited language-model loss-scaling studies, it does not fit loss against parameters, training tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The evaluated quantity varies with in-context demonstration count; no sensitivity analysis of loss-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: After continued pretraining on synthetic tabular tasks, accuracy rises monotonically with in-context demonstrations: 58.4 at 8 shots to 75.3 at 512, with further gains up to 1,024. Vanilla LLMs gain much less: GPT-5-mini +4.7, Qwen-7B +8.3, and o3-mini about +1.8 with a dip at 128 shots.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy scales with the number of in-context demonstrations (many-shot ICL scaling), and the strength of this scaling depends on training.

record.problems: The results relevant to V6 are aggregate accuracy values rather than held-out cross-entropy, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these values. The tested scaling variable is demonstration count, not model size, pretraining tokens, or compute.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 also reports KNN, Random Forest, and TabICL results; those non-LLM baselines are not extracted here. Per-task results in Tables 3, 6, and 7 are also omitted because the aggregate Table 2 comparisons capture the reported demonstration-count scaling relevant to V6; these tables do not test the specified language-model loss laws.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss fit on small runs extrapolated to larger runs.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in another modality or regime. Continued pretraining is reported without a loss-versus-scale curve.
No downstream performance versus model size, pretraining tokens, compute or pretraining loss. Only one 7B backbone is used.
No analysis of fitted exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link conflated in-context shot count with 'scale'. V6 concerns scale in model size, data or compute, or in pretraining loss. The paper fits no power law even for shots; it only reports monotonic increase. The Table 2 values are transcribed correctly.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No loss-law fit on small runs or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or comparison of parameter and token scaling.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No test of the stated power-law form across modalities or training regimes.
The study tests accuracy as in-context demonstration count increases, not downstream performance as model parameter count, pretraining tokens, compute, or pretraining loss changes.
No analysis of fitted exponents, fit choices, or departures from a single power law for loss.
